extracted.intended_audience: Recipients of federal education funding (K-12 school districts, colleges and universities), Title IX coordinators, investigators, and institutional administrators responsible for Title IX compliance
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory guidance on use and limits of informal resolution (including restorative justice) under §106.45(b)(9) and on recordkeeping requirements under §106.45(b)(10), including retention periods, scope of records to preserve, parties' access, and related procedural safeguards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient autonomy to use restorative justice as informal resolution
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in §106.45(b)(9) prohibits recipients from using restorative justice as an informal resolution process to address sexual misconduct incidents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restorative justice's requirement that a respondent admit responsibility at the start does not necessarily mean the recipient has reached a determination of responsibility; participation must be voluntary. A recipient may specify whether an admission during restorative justice will be used in adjudication if parties later resume the formal grievance process. Recipients may also use restorative justice after a determination of responsibility; the regulations do not dictate the form of disciplinary sanction a recipient may impose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Informal resolution may be offered only after a formal complaint is filed
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient may not offer informal resolution unless a formal complaint has been filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures parties are aware of the allegations at issue and the formal procedures that will apply absent informal resolution, and prevents recipients from avoiding formal grievance procedures altogether.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voluntary participation and written consent for informal resolution
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may never require participation in informal resolution and may not require students or employees to waive their rights to a §106.45 grievance process as a condition of enrollment or employment, or enjoyment of any other right.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both parties must provide voluntary written consent to informal resolution. Either party may withdraw from the informal resolution process and resume the formal grievance process at any time prior to agreeing to a resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipients may limit types and formats of informal resolution
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.45(b)(9) does not preclude a recipient from categorically refusing to offer and facilitate an informal process that involves the parties directly interacting, from prohibiting a facilitator from directly questioning parties, or from requiring the parties to be in separate rooms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients have discretion to design informal processes they deem appropriate and may restrict facilitator practices or formats (e.g., no face-to-face mediation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Method of obtaining consent and disclosures (electronic permitted)
rubrics_metrics.description: The final regulations do not specify the method of delivery for written notices and disclosures, including the method by which the recipient must obtain parties' voluntary written consent to informal resolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients have discretion to use electronic disclosures and signatures; the Department acknowledges convenience, privacy, and security benefits of electronic methods but does not mandate them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expulsion and severe sanctions may be part of informal resolution only by agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department will not prohibit recipients from using informal resolution where it results in expulsion; if expulsion is proposed as part of an informal resolution, that result can only occur if both parties agree to the resolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a respondent does not agree to an expulsion proposed in informal resolution, the respondent can withdraw and resume the formal grievance process that may result in investigation, adjudication, and disciplinary sanction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipients must maintain records of each sexual harassment investigation for seven years
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 106.45(b)(10) requires recipients to maintain records of 'each sexual harassment investigation.' Any record that the recipient creates to investigate an allegation, regardless of later dismissal or other resolution of the allegation, must be maintained for seven years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department extended the retention period from three years (proposed) to seven years to harmonize with the Clery Act and address commenters' concerns about inadequate retention. Recipients may retain records longer if desired or required by other legal obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of records to preserve (including truncated investigations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must preserve all records created to investigate an allegation, including records from truncated investigations that led to no adjudication because the acts alleged did not constitute sex discrimination under Title IX and the formal complaint (or allegation therein) was dismissed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Records include any documentation created during investigation; questions raised by commenters about what specific documents (transcripts, lists of steps, training materials, etc.) should be kept prompted clarification that investigative records must be preserved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parties' access to records and confidentiality of supportive measures
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department revised §106.45(b)(10)(i) to remove the language making records available to parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties continue to receive written notice of allegations, the evidence directly related to the allegations, the investigative report, and the written determination, and have the right to inspect and review the recording or transcript of a live hearing. Removing the broader access requirement protects confidentiality of supportive measures and remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipients' discretion on sanctions and consideration of deliberate indifference law
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department declines to mandate suspension or expulsion as the only appropriate sanction following a determination of responsibility; recipients deserve flexibility to design sanctions that best reflect their educational mission and community and the unique circumstances of each case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients may consider relevant Title IX case law (deliberate indifference standards) and other legal obligations when determining sanctions; courts have found deliberate indifference in some circumstances but do not require uniform suspension/expulsion for every responsible finding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retention period should accommodate state-law and special circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: Although the final regulations standardize a seven-year minimum retention period, nothing prevents recipients from keeping records longer if required by State statute or other obligations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters urged linking retention to statutes of limitations, student enrollment duration, or Clery Act requirements; the Department chose a standardized seven-year minimum to simplify compliance while noting recipients may adopt longer retention (e.g., ten years or indefinite) where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uncertainty and questions about timing for retention clock and types of records
rubrics_metrics.description: Commenters asked when the clock begins (date of incident, date reported, or conclusion of complaint) and what types of records must be kept (transcripts, lists of steps, training materials).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final regulation's requirement that each sexual harassment investigation record be maintained for seven years addresses retention length; recipients should preserve records created as part of investigations. Questions about precise start points and particular document categories were raised and should be considered when drafting institutional policies to ensure compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training materials retention and transparency expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Many commenters requested that recipients' Title IX training materials be made publicly available and that training materials be archived to allow assessment for fairness and absence of bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters urged requiring archiving only for material changes rather than minor edits; some recommended keeping training summaries rather than full materials to reduce burden on smaller recipients. The Department's recordkeeping revisions (seven-year retention) and other provisions reflect concern for training quality and transparency, though precise archival granularity may be left to recipients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data collection requests and optional reporting elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Commenters suggested recipients collect additional data (dates, cross-complaints, notifications, demographics, outcomes, sanctions, legal costs, settlements) and some requested that recipients send records to the Department annually.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While commenters requested broad data collection to evaluate disparate impacts and system performance, the Department did not adopt a requirement to submit all such data; recipients may consider collecting additional data to improve internal accountability but should be mindful of privacy and other legal constraints.
